findings.identity_proportions: Neet retains a substantial narrow ribcage, visible raised neck, four fine legs, broad triangular ears, pale muzzle/bib and a tiny rump nub. The head remains modest and the torso is not hollowed.
findings.anatomy_support: Both forelegs join the chest and both rear legs join the pelvis; four individual paws contact the cobbles with coherent shadows. No disconnected or additional limb. Low camera perspective is consistent between dog, bananas and post.
findings.grooming_finish: Broad tan paint shapes cover the torso and thighs. Restrained edge/neck marks do not form curled body patterns, raised shag or added coat volume. Smooth silhouette and clean paws; no material patterned-coat defect.
findings.scene_continuity_comedy: Fallen bananas are beside Neet; the wooden signpost is empty and his serious upward gaze makes the needless final defense readable. No premature cabbage or rewards. The background vendors and Indian market setting fit this beat; other participants may be outside this focused framing.

findings.identity_proportions: Buddy has a continuous moderately elongated charcoal torso, visible neck, substantial legs with real ground clearance, pale muzzle/brows/lower legs and hanging ears. The tapered dark tail joins the rump and does not become a plume.
findings.anatomy_support: Four leg roots and four paws are readable and grounded. The woman sits on the crate with draped legs and visible supported feet; both hands connect through wrists to their own arms. Buddy nose sits immediately beneath the lowered fingers without fused anatomy.
findings.grooming_finish: The replacement has smooth broad charcoal torso and thigh fields and a smooth back outline. Furnishings remain concentrated at muzzle, brows, ears and feet, with limited underside fringe corresponding to B29; it does not create enlarged shag body volume. No curly engraved torso pattern.
findings.scene_continuity_comedy: The older tomato seller, scattered tomatoes and single tomato near her crate match Buddy returning to her hand. Her slight smile and his attention deliver the quiet emotional counterpoint. The sari-clad vendor is provisional, not Heather; no rewards appear early. Market and evening light remain coherent.

findings.identity_proportions: Both named dogs remain distinct: Neet has fine legs, narrow full trunk, broad ears and nub; Buddy has a longer dark torso, substantial legs, furnished pale face and tapered tail. The front three-quarter view shortens Buddy apparent length without collapsing his torso.
findings.anatomy_support: Neet has four owned limbs, with one front paw deliberately occluded inside the cabbage leaf; its foreleg enters the leaf naturally at ground level. Buddy has four grounded paws and continuous chest-to-pelvis construction. No merged or floating limb.
findings.grooming_finish: The retained composition now uses smooth broad body colors on both dogs. Buddy face and ears carry regional strands, while torso and upper legs have no repeated curling fur pattern or raised shag contour. The leaf veins are prop detail, not coat texture.
findings.scene_continuity_comedy: The cabbage leaf wraps Neet front paw beside the reward basket; Buddy biscuit lies at his feet. Neet solemn stance and Buddy downward attention support the flair joke. Basket contents can be partially occluded; the close framing does not imply Shadow, Chikki or vendors have left. Evening produce stalls maintain the historical setting.
